**THE POSITION**


**This recruitment is being conducted to fill three full\-time vacancies. The list established by this recruitment may be used to fill future full\-time, part\-time, limited term, and temporary vacancies for up to one year.**


This position exists to provide timely and accurate assistance to the Housing Authority of the City of Vallejo (HACV) Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) program participants in a manner that provides excellent customer service and meets HUD regulations and HACV policies. The incumbent in this position performs initial and ongoing eligibility determinations; inspect units prior to occupancy by HCV participants and while participants are residing in the units; conducts landlord outreach; monitors and determines local rental housing rates and negotiate rental agreements; conducts investigations; conducts new participant briefings; prepares and maintains technical and confidential documents; represents the City and the VHA in a positive and professional manner; and completes other housing\-related tasks. This position may also serve as the HCV Family Self\-Sufficiency Coordinator.


The ideal candidate for this position will demonstrate a strong work ethic, communicate effectively, are customer service oriented, is able to work both independently and in a team environment, is a problem solver and critical thinker, respects and values others, and should understand the organization and operation of the City and outside agencies.

The Housing and Community Development (HCD) Department manages programs funded by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD). The HCD Division also provides staff support to the Housing and Community Development Commission.

The City of Vallejo is located in Solano County and has a population of approximately 121,000 residents. It is a friendly, active waterfront community that attracts innovative, hardworking people and takes great pride in its 148\-year history and maritime heritage. Residents of Vallejo are situated to take advantage of the best of what the area has to offer. Golf, museums, performing arts, boutique shopping, brewpubs and a wide selection of restaurants are all available in Vallejo. Residents and visitors alike enjoy Vallejo’s delightful historical downtown area, weekly downtown farmer’s market, and beautifully restored Victorian homes and business facades. Vallejo is also home to Six Flags Discovery Kingdom, one of America’s only combination wildlife, oceanarium and theme parks.

**Company Overview**
====================


For more than 50 years, Insight Housing has provided a comprehensive range of housing, food, and support services to help those in need move from homelessness into a safe and affordable home of their own. We serve in seven counties in the bay area \- Alameda, San Francisco, Contra Costa, Solano, Sacramento, San Joaquin, and Amador County. We are proud of our team members who are very dedicated to our mission *of ensuring everyone in our community has a home through supportive, equitable, and sustainable housing solutions.***Program Overview**
====================

**Shelter Plus Care** (S\+C): Funded by the City of Berkeley, the Shelter Plus Care program provides permanent supportive housing to adults who are chronically homeless and living with disabilities, including substance use disorders, mental illness, dual diagnosis, and/or HIV/AIDS, who have been prioritized through the Alameda County Coordinated Entry System. Participants receive a rental subsidy paired with ongoing supportive services, including housing navigation, tenancy sustaining services, home visits, life skills counseling, benefits advocacy, and case management.

**Berkeley Respite**: Also funded by the City of Berkeley, the Berkeley Respite Program is a temporary shelter and intensive housing navigation program serving eight households experiencing homelessness across two shelter homes in Berkeley. Respite is not permanent housing; residents work closely with a Case Manager toward permanent housing, income, and independence, with progress reviewed weekly, monthly, and quarterly.

**Position Summary**
====================


Under the supervision of the Program Manager, the Housing Case Manager carries a blended caseload across two City of Berkeley–funded programs: approximately 11 Shelter Plus Care participants and 8 households in the Berkeley Respite Program. Shelter Plus Care caseload size is approximate and may fluctuate based on referrals, placements, and contract requirements. For Shelter Plus Care participants, the Housing Case Manager provides housing navigation for those not yet placed and tenancy sustaining services for those in permanent housing, conducting regular home visits throughout Berkeley and Alameda County. For Respite residents, permanent housing placement is the primary goal of every stay: the Housing Case Manager drives an active housing search with each household, builds landlord relationships, removes housing barriers, and supports lease\-up and move\-in, while also overseeing day\-to\-day operations of the two shelter homes. * Maintain a caseload of approximately 11 Shelter Plus Care participants housed throughout Berkeley and Alameda County; caseload size may fluctuate based on referrals, placements, and contract requirements.
* Coordinate the participant intake process; conduct initial assessment and eligibility determination for new referrals received through the Coordinated Entry System; create and maintain participant files electronically in a timely manner.

We are proud of our team members who are very dedicated to our mission *of ensuring everyone in our community has a home through supportive, equitable, and sustainable housing solutions.***Program Overview**
====================

**Albany Project Hope**: Since July 2013, Insight Housing has provided street outreach and housing navigation to residents of the City of Albany experiencing homelessness. Outreach is the core of the program: staff conduct daily field\-based outreach routes throughout Albany to engage unsheltered residents, complete Coordinated Entry System (CES) assessments, and connect people to housing and services. The program also operates one 4\-bedroom master\-leased transitional home providing shelter for up to four households through December 2026; the home is scheduled to close January 1, 2027, after which the program transitions to full\-time street outreach and housing navigation. Services are delivered using Housing First, Harm Reduction, Trauma\-Informed Care, and Progressive Engagement models. Insight Housing serves as a key CES access point for the City of Albany and works in close partnership with Albany CARES, the Albany Police Department, and regional homeless service providers.

**Position Summary**
====================


Under the supervision of the Program Manager, the Housing Navigator is responsible for street outreach, engagement, housing navigation, and case management for Albany residents experiencing homelessness. This is a field\-based position: the majority of the workday is spent outdoors on assigned outreach routes, engaging unsheltered residents where they are rather than working from an office. The Housing Navigator builds trusting relationships through consistent, persistent engagement, completes CES assessments, develops housing stability plans, and supports participants through housing search, placement, and retention. Through January 2027, the Housing Navigator also provides case management to residents of the program’s emergency shelter house and supports their transition to permanent housing prior to the home’s closure.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**
=========================================

* Conduct daily, field\-based street outreach along assigned routes throughout the City of Albany — including the community center, the senior center, the areas around the Safeway and Target stores, Albany Hill, the shower program at the Albany Aquatic Center, Solano and San Pablo Avenues, and the Ohlone Greenway — and other locations where people experiencing homelessness congregate.
* Build and sustain trusting relationships with unsheltered residents through consistent, persistent engagement, using Housing First, Harm Reduction, Trauma\-Informed Care, and Progressive Engagement approaches.
* Distribute outreach and basic needs supplies, including hygiene items, weather\-appropriate clothing, water, and snacks.
* Respond to outreach referrals and crisis requests from City of Albany staff, Albany CARES, the Albany Police Department, and community partners.
* Assist participants in meeting basic needs for food, shelter, medical and mental health care, identification documents, and benefits enrollment.
* Complete Coordinated Entry System (CES) assessments for all consenting participants engaged through outreach.
* Develop and update individual housing stability plans at least every 90 days for all engaged program participants.
* Monitor CES prioritization lists, advocate for timely permanent housing matches, and attend regional CES case conferences and matching meetings.
* Provide ongoing housing search and navigation support, including obtaining identification documents, applying for and maintaining income, addressing past evictions or poor credit, and building independent living skills.
* Make referrals and linkages to medical care, mental health and substance use treatment, benefits enrollment, legal services, employment services, domestic violence services, and veterans services; coordinate warm handoffs to permanent supportive housing providers upon match.
* Administer flexible housing support funds for barrier removal: transportation assistance, document fees, emergency clothing and food, and essential household items, consistent with participant housing stability plans and agency financial procedures.

* Prepare monthly and quarterly statistical and narrative program reports for the City of Albany, and provide accurate participant and outreach data as needed by the Program Manager.

**Job Description**
-------------------


The Patient Care Coordinator supports patients in their designated team with an emphasis on care coordination. As a co\-located member of the team, will coordinate the registry of patients and activates them to ensure adherence to care pathways. Will be assigned respective duties to their department.
Duties and Responsibilities:


* Supports patients in meeting their care goals and adhering to their pertinent care plan.
* Conducts telephonic or electronic outreach to patients requiring follow\-up on their care plan, in order to ensure continuity of accurate care.
* Engages patients in becoming active members in their care plan by using motivational interviewing techniques.
* Grooms provider schedules to ensure appropriate visit interventions.
* Coordinates and attends patient case conferences with appropriate providers. Handles any follow\-up task emerging from case conferences.
* Updates provider goals and care plans, if needed, to allow for visibility by entire care team.
* Accomplishes pharmacist orders to ensure adherence to pharmacist drug therapy plan, if the patient is enrolled in Drug Therapy Management (DTM).
* Complete care coordination orders for patients as determined by provider, care manager, and social work and maintains a daily management tracking system.
* Schedules pertinent provider appointments such as primary care, specialty, procedures, etc.
* Ensures all discharge orders are completed per discharge plan or providers' order in accordance with their care plan.
* Assists in verifying health plan benefits for any ordered services.
* Remains available to assist with visit checkout for patients to ensure all needs are addressed prior to leaving clinic.
* Will be assigned to patients and will follow with any issue process to address non\-adherence or any other patient concerns.
* Coordinates and attends patient case conferences with appropriate providers. Attends to any follow\-up task emerging from case conferences.
* Performs pharmacist orders to ensure adherence to pharmacist drug therapy plan, if the patient is enrolled in Drug Therapy Management (DTM).

**Job Description**

Under the supervision of the Director of Quality and Patient Safety, the Disease\-Specific Care Coordinator functions as an expert nurse in the disease specific field, resource for nursing staff and patient care in this area, consultant, researcher and outcomes focused specialist. The Coordinator is responsible for providing coordination and oversight for the assigned hospital’s disease\-specific program. This multidimensional role will focus on current treatment, prevention, education to improve quality of patient care. The Coordinator will drive current certification through performance improvement activities and standard compliance. Regularly performs tasks to ensure efficient operations of all aspects for the disease\-specific program. Serves as a liaison between quality improvement, nursing and medical staff in the disease\-specific program at SVH. This position is responsible for reporting and presenting accurate, quality information both internally and externally. Responsible for site compliance: reviews source documentation case report forms, data reports for accuracy, and ensures timely submission of such documentation to assure timely compliance with program requirements. Has primary responsibility for leading, controlling, planning, organizing and evaluating the timely, effective and efficient function of the program data and standards. They collaborate in the implementation of multidisciplinary standards for patient with disease\-specific care and promote effective control mechanisms to ensure that the physical environment fosters safe patient care. Collaborates in planning, implementing, and evaluating department activities including appropriate knowledge of PI practice and theory to assure professional competency to ensure care is evidence based.  



  

The Coordinator acts as a role model, preceptor of staff, ensures the consistent application of the Hospital’s policies and procedures and fosters teamwork within and between areas of responsibility. The Coordinator is also responsible for promoting and participating in specialized knowledge and skills through the support of staff education and professional development. As a clinical resource to clinical and medical staff in providing in\-services, and advising management on training needs. The Coordinator acts as an effective liaison to medical staff to ensure continuity and congruity of hospital services in accordance with the plan of care.  



  

* Facilitates and coordinates program development in order to maintain Joint Commission Disease\-Specific Certification, or accreditation by other certifying agencies (i.e., Society of Cardiovascular Patient Care \[SCPC]).
* Applies the quality improvement process to implement and evaluate quality of care and make recommendations for implementation of new technology or change in disease\-specific care, treatment, management and prevention practices.
* Assists with development and implementation of programs to support the needs of patients and their families and goals of the Disease\-Specific Program. Participates in relevant quality and performance improvements.
* Assists in the development of appropriate educational material for patients, family, and clinical staff in collaboration with Education, Nursing/Clinical and Medical Staff.
* Initiates and performs ongoing review of policies and protocols related to services provided to ensure standards are followed. When appropriate, updates or writes new policies to enhance professional practice.
* Promotes and participates in improving patient care and in quality performance improvement programs by taking primary responsibility for data collection and analysis of results to support the nursing departments.
* Assist in ongoing clinical performance audits in the clinical departments in order to ensure regulatory compliance, promote patient safety and establish quality outcomes.
* Facilitates collection of, analyzes and presents disease\-specific certification program data and research at appropriate physician and clinical meetings. Uses data to set benchmarks for hospital performance improvement programs.
* Serves as a resource/liaison for staff assigned to assist with disease\-specific care research and data collection as needed. Trains data entry and data acquisition personnel as needed.
* Designs, tests, documents and maintains an audit process for data quality validation.
* Mentors staff in the understanding of disease\-specific care and research in quality improvement for patient population. Assists staff to use evidence\-based outcome data to improve patient care.
* Assures that complete and accurate data is collected, calculated and documented. Maintains integrity of data security, confidentiality and preservation for the control and use of program information.
* Attends and participates in the committees that relate to the Disease\-Specific Care Program.
* Consistently provides timely accurate reports and updates to the Leadership Team, the Medical Staff committees and the Quality and Safety Committee as appropriate.
* Communicates any patient\-related clinical issues or problems of the department requiring additional assistance to the Director and/or Manager immediately and to the Senior Administrative Director of Regulatory Compliance \& Organizational Improvement.
* Maintains an active role in outcome data management of the Disease\-Specific Program. Ensures that certification requirements for data submission are met.

**Medical Center:** Community Health Partnership\- (Full\-Time, Day Shift) \-
  
  

**Job Summary:** The Community Health Worker is responsible for helping patients and their families navigate and access community services, access health care services, and adopt healthy behaviors. Supports providers and the care management teams through an integrated approach to case management and community outreach. Provides social support and informal counseling, as well as advocate for individuals and community health needs. Assists clinical personnel with community outreach, such as home visits, assists with health assessments, and involvement in various clinical\-community intervention activities will be required when assigned. Performs other duties as needed.
  
  

**Education and Experience:** One year of experience working in a community based setting preferred.
  
  

**Knowledge and Skills:** Experience working in a multi\-cultural setting. Knowledgeable about community resources appropriate to needs of patients/families and provide referrals for services to community agencies as appropriate. Knowledge of basic medical terminology preferred. Able to read; write legibly; speak in English and Spanish fluently with professional quality; use computer, printer, and software programs necessary to the position (e.g., Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint). Operate/troubleshoot basic office and patient care equipment required for the position; perform required patient care activities related to the position. Able to relate and communicate positively, effectively, and professionally with others; work calmly and respond courteously when under pressure; collaborate and accept direction. Able to communicate effectively in English in person, in writing, and on the telephone; think critically; manage multiple assignments effectively; organize and prioritize workload; work well under pressure; problem solve; recall information with accuracy; pay close attention to detail; work independently with minimal supervision. Able to distinguish colors as necessary; hear sufficiently for general conversation in person and on the telephone, and identify and distinguish various sounds associated with the workplace; see adequately to read computer screens, and written documents necessary to the position.
  
  

**Licensures and Certifications:** Valid Driver's License required at time of hire. Successful completion of a Community Health Worker formal training program such as from a college or other education institution is preferred.
